content: The object is located at a distance of 285 kilometers, with a resolution of 3 meters per pixel. The left image has been rotated 90 degrees relative to the right image. The right image represents the front view of the left side, which is just out of view in the left image. The object rotates according to the right-hand rule, transitioning from the orientation in the left image to that in the right image. The surface of the rocky object appears pitted or cratered, a result of the evaporation of volatile materials. Short-period comets are characterized by orbital periods of less than 20 years and low orbital inclinations. These comets are influenced by Jupiter's gravitational field, leading to their classification as Jupiter Family Comets. Because their orbits intersect with that of Jupiter, these comets experience gravitational interactions with the massive planet. Over time, these interactions alter the comet's orbit, potentially resulting in the comet being ejected from the Solar System, colliding with a planet, or falling into the Sun. Sedimentology involves the study of modern sediments, such as sand, mud (silt), and clay, as well as the processes that lead to their deposition. Sedimentary rocks, which cover the majority of Earth's surface, serve as a record of much of Earth's history and contain the fossil record. Sedimentology is closely related to stratigraphy, which examines the physical and temporal relationships between rock layers or strata. Structural geology focuses on the three-dimensional distribution of rock units and their deformational histories. For example, the image on the right depicts rock strata in Cafayate, Argentina, which is a subject of stratigraphic study. One hypothesis suggests that geological forces observed on Earth should also apply to astronomical objects composed of rock. The content on this page was initially contributed by Henry A. Hoff.
